input.task: List all the authors quoted in this thread.

provenance: M38, the second negative — the twin of resolver-narrows-identical-matches, same page, same target, same three interchangeable matches, and the task wording is the ONLY difference. A plural request answered from one of several matches is the failure `extract_all` exists to prevent: the run would report one author, in the right shape, for a question that asked for the set — `success`, grounded, anchored, and wrong by omission with nothing in the trace to say so. So the document-order rung is refused whenever the task asks for more than one thing, and the run fails loudly for the planner to fix with `extract_all` instead. Watched red by ablation: with the plural test removed from the rung's guard, this case reports `status success, answer 'Marisol Vance'` for 'List all the authors quoted in this thread.'

triage.what_this_grades: the singular-wording conjunct of the document-order rung, which no other case can exercise: rung 2's positive twin differs from this case in the task string alone. The `extract_all` path never reaches this code (`many=True` returns the whole match set by design), so this guard only ever fires on a plan that reached for `extract` when the task asked for a set — a planner defect (M32), caught here rather than answered.
triage.ceiling: a regex over English plural asks (all/every/each/both/list/how many/which ones/names of), the same ceiling as SCOPE_BLOCK and _AGGREGATE and widened the same way: when a probe finds the next phrasing, not by guessing at synonyms nobody has seen. A plural task phrased outside it falls through to the rung and is answered from the first match.
